page.layout: One printed page. Running head with page number at top: "244" and "Animalium Mar. Ordo XV." Below it a full-width italic paragraph. Then two woodcut figures (A left, B right) with a text block below, a German note in black letter beneath the first text, a second text block at left with a German note beneath, a large woodcut figure at right and another at lower left; a catchword-like word "MVREX" at the lower right is a signature-like mark placed at the foot right.

main_text.head: Animalium Mar. Ordo XV.

p.i: A. iconem Rondeletius exhibuit: cui nos similem alteram B. adiunximus, Conchae cuiusdam seu Muricis orientalis, quam Venetijs nacti sumus, in ea margaritas quoque gigni quidam nobis retulit, nescio quàm vere. Color forinsecus pallescit, intrinsecus cum pulcherrimo splendore ex albo roseus est. Labrum exterius protendit se & dilatat in marginem. Mucrones infra caput seu conum testae duo magni, sed obtusi, prominet, in ipso cono parvi admodum & subrotundi, per spiras deinceps, non aculei sed tumores visuntur.

main_text.p: MVREX Marmoreus Rondeletio dictus, à candore duritiáque, qua marmor (inquit) candidum aemulatur parte externa: parte interna ex albo purpurascit.

p.bl: GERM. Ein art & Stachelschnecke/außwendig weyß wie ein marmel/inwendig leybfarb.

main_text.p: MVREX Triangularis Rondeletij. Hic altera parte (inquit) Murex planus est, altera fere rotundus: sed ita ut utrinque duo sint latera, tertiū plana pars efficiat: à qua figura, quae huic propria est, triangularis iure dicitur. Vario est colore. Foramen duplex habet, rugosum: quo ob testae amplitudinem et brevitatem, sonus editur gravis et tristis. Testa tota ad Conchylij testā magis accedit.

p.bl: GERM. Ein andere art der Stachelschnecke mit try ecken an & schalē.

page.notes: Figures A, B, and the two lower woodcuts of shells are not transcribed as text. The German black-letter lines are rendered in black letter markup. Some words are uncertain in the scan, notably the German lines and the Latin edge words; the marked signature "MVREX" at the lower right is treated as a foot mark.
